issue_context.title: USB GET_INTERFACE response always 0, even when an alternate setting is used
comments:
First of all, whats the use case to add alternate setting for such device?
In order to make it work i suppose that [custom_handler](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/class/loopback.c#L169) must be implemented but I might be wrong as I took only i brief look into this. I cannot say when I will have time to do it as I am a bit busy right now and I do not see clear use case for that right now.
The current code is indeed incorrect but for all the classes and functionalities we support just right now its sufficient. 
Alternate settings are commonly used in audio class. Implementation could be found here #21526.
I think it would be worthwhile to implement it in audio for sure and as an author I will keep that in mind as for now it is missing.

Sorry for being a bit unclear - the example was just the quickest way I could find to create a patch that would fail in the USB compliance test. I'm tinkering with audio stuff and it was in that context that the issue was found. 

I can create a PR for a more generic solution; store the alternate setting after a successful USB SET_INTERFACE and returning that in the GET_INTERFACE request.
Ah, okay now I get this. If You want to post a PR it would be great. One question as You said 'generic solution'. Where do You gonna store the info about alternate setting?
Good question. If zephyr only supports one interface would it be out of place to store it in struct usb_dev_priv?

Until now it supported no alternate settings but many interfaces. For example if You configure 2x cdc there will be 4 interfaces in total. 

It cant be in usb_dev_priv as on this level You are not possible to guess the total number of interfaces so there is no possibility to create a table or whatsoever to store this information.
I think the only way now is to implement [custom_handler](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/include/usb/usb_device.h#L161) as it is called prio the [std_interface_req()](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/usb_device.c#L914), but this will get tricky as well because of how the set_interface is handled..
We can follow up on Slack, feel free to ping me there.
